title: People illustration / Rose and Almond — CMYK palette

location.series: IBM Design Language / alternate tab states
location.label: CMYK

slide_intent: Preserve the range of human representation across print production, because a digital specimen alone does not specify its ink mixture.
strategic_value: Recorded process-color builds can help IBM’s people illustrations retain their intended tonal distinctions in print.
demonstration: The CMYK tab presents ten Rose and ten Almond grades with cyan, magenta, yellow and black values in two parallel columns.
practical_value: Use the supplied process build for a chosen people-palette grade when preparing print illustration.

content_islands.name: Encoding selector
content_islands.spec: Show CMYK selected in the three-tab control.

content_islands.name: Rose process builds
content_islands.spec: List the Rose family from 100 to 10 with four ink-channel values.

content_islands.name: Almond process builds
content_islands.spec: Place the corresponding Almond grade sequence alongside it.

reference_purposes.Expression: Parallel Rose and Almond ramps show the palette’s tonal range.
reference_purposes.Application: The selected tab supplies CMYK builds for all twenty people-palette entries.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The accompanying People guidance reserves these colors for skin, hair and nails, rather than broadening the main IBM palette.
